newsitem.title: USA: DSC Comms, Westell in ADSL pact.
newsitem.headline: DSC Comms, Westell in ADSL pact.

text.p: DSC Communications Corp and Westell Technologies Inc said they had signed a joint development deal to intergrate Westell's broadband access technology into DSC's new phone carrier local loop system.
The announcement, which was made Wednesday, would combine Westell's ADSL (Asymmetrical Digital Subscriber Line) product with DSC's Litespan-2000 Next Generation Digital Loop Carrier (NGDLC) platform.
A DSC spokesman said the deal will create a low-cost, high-speed broadband system for use on existing phone company systems. Specific terms of the deal were not disclosed.
Industry analysts believe the deal will accelerate the move by major U.S. phone companies and Internet Service Providers to offer high-speed broadband services over existing copper wire lines.
The initial ADSL product is ideal for Internet access and work-at-home applications, while also providing a path to simultaneous video and data services, the companies said.
In their joint statement, the companies did not reveal when the Westell equipment, which would essentially run as an application on existing DSC equipment, would be available.
Asked what date the first products might be deployed by customers, DSC spokesman Terry Adams declined to comment.
"We are certainly making this product visible to our customers," Adams said. "We will be talking more about that in the coming months and weeks."
Adams said DSC had not agreed to make Westell its exclusive supplier of ADSL technology. DSC will partner with other ADSL suppliers if customers demand it, he said.
DSC Litespan's digital loop platform accounted for about $500 million, or one-third of DSC's total 1996 revenues of $1.4 billion, according to Adams.
DSC also provides switching and transport products to a base made up largely of carriers.
The two companies said the deal will allow them to deliver a fully integrated, end-to-end ADSL system which will enable simple, cost-effective upgrades for existing Litespan customers.

DSC's Litespan is used by six of the seven U.S. Baby Bell companies, and various smaller independents, as a means for connecting local telephone customers to the phone company's community-based central office switches.

The product's top three customers are Bell Atlantic Corp, NYNEX Corp and Ameritech Corp. Bell Atlantic and NYNEX, which are in a deal to be merged, alone control roughly 40 percent of all U.S. phone access lines.

DSC and Westell also said they are developing an ADSL line unit for DSC's Litespan that has Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) capabilities running at up to 155 megabits per second along the backbone transport layer of phone company networks.
By combining the ADSL transport with ATM, DSC and Westell can provide a cost- effective, end-to-end solution across copper pair wire, they said.

The Litespan ADSL capability can be added without interruption to existing narrowband services. This minimal hardware requirement greatly reduces time-to-market and start-up costs, the companies said.
